question.problem: Consider the surface $xy{z}^{2}=6-z.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(1,1,2).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}xy{z}^{2} & =6-z \\ xy{z}^{2}+z & =6\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=xy{z}^{2}+z$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=6.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }k \\  & =(y{z}^{2})\text{ }i+(x{z}^{2})\text{ }j+(2xyz+1)\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,2) & =(1)(2)^{2}\text{ }i+(1)(2)^{2}\text{ }j+(2(1)(1)(2)+1)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i+4j+5\,k \\  & =⟨4,4,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,4,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-1)+4(y-1)+5(z-2) & =0 \\ 4x+4y+5z-18 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
